t: #2199 Finding the Topic of Each Post
o: We must label each post with the sorted, deduplicated list of topic IDs whose keywords appear (case-insensitively, as whole words) in the post content, or "Ambiguous!" if none match. In example 1, post 3 contains both "war" (topic 3) and "handball" (topic 1), producing "1,3"; post 4 contains "warning" and "vaccinated" but neither equals a keyword, so it is ambiguous. Since content contains only letters and spaces, whole-word matching can be done by comparing against space-delimited tokens. Content lengths are small, so even a cross join with a LIKE per keyword is fine.
k: Wrap the content with spaces and match '% word %' to guarantee whole-word, case-insensitive matches.
LEFT JOIN + GROUP_CONCAT(DISTINCT ... ORDER BY ...) naturally yields NULL (mapped to 'Ambiguous!') when no keyword matches.
Alternatively, tokenize each post into words with SUBSTRING_INDEX and join on exact equality.

a.n: Approach 1: LIKE join with word boundaries
a.i: Join every post to every keyword whose lowercase form appears as a space-bounded token in the lowercase content. Grouping by post and aggregating distinct topic IDs in order gives the answer; posts with no match survive the LEFT JOIN with NULL, which we translate to 'Ambiguous!'.
s: Wrap content with surrounding spaces and lowercase it.
LEFT JOIN Keywords on content LIKE CONCAT('% ', LOWER(word), ' %').
Group by post_id and aggregate DISTINCT topic_id ordered ascending.
Replace NULL aggregates with 'Ambiguous!' using IFNULL/COALESCE.

c.python:
-- SQL (MySQL)
SELECT p.post_id,
       IFNULL(GROUP_CONCAT(DISTINCT k.topic_id ORDER BY k.topic_id), 'Ambiguous!') AS topic
FROM Posts p
LEFT JOIN Keywords k
  ON LOWER(CONCAT(' ', p.content, ' ')) LIKE CONCAT('% ', LOWER(k.word), ' %')
GROUP BY p.post_id;

a.n: Approach 2: Tokenize words, then exact-match join
a.i: Split each post into its individual words using SUBSTRING_INDEX driven by a numbers sequence, lowercase them, and join to Keywords on equality. Exact equality avoids any substring false positives by construction.
s: Generate numbers 1..maxWords with a recursive CTE.
Extract the nth space-separated word of each post with nested SUBSTRING_INDEX.
Join words to Keywords on LOWER(word) = extracted word.
Aggregate DISTINCT topic_id per post; coalesce to 'Ambiguous!'.

c.python:
-- SQL (MySQL 8)
WITH RECURSIVE seq AS (
  SELECT 1 AS n UNION ALL SELECT n+1 FROM seq WHERE n < 100
), words AS (
  SELECT p.post_id,
         LOWER(SUBSTRING_INDEX(SUBSTRING_INDEX(CONCAT(p.content, ' '), ' ', s.n), ' ', -1)) AS w
  FROM Posts p
  JOIN seq s
    ON s.n <= LENGTH(p.content) - LENGTH(REPLACE(p.content, ' ', '')) + 1
)
SELECT w.post_id,
       IFNULL(GROUP_CONCAT(DISTINCT k.topic_id ORDER BY k.topic_id), 'Ambiguous!') AS topic
FROM words w
LEFT JOIN Keywords k ON LOWER(k.word) = w.w
GROUP BY w.post_id;

w: Use the LIKE approach for brevity; the tokenizing approach is more robust if matching rules grow stricter. Pitfalls: forgetting case-insensitivity, matching prefixes like 'war' inside 'warning', duplicate topic IDs in the output, and forgetting the LEFT JOIN so ambiguous posts disappear. Follow-ups: multi-word phrases, ranking topics by number of matched keywords.
